center.locator: The surface detector array of the Telescope Array experiment, site-description section
center.note: Map centre only; not a claim about any structure. Uses the array's own published coordinate.
center.quote: The TA site is located in the desert about 1400 m above sea level centered at 39.3 N and 112.9 W in Millard County, Utah, USA

levels.name: Surface
levels.note: The array is entirely at the surface.

name: Telescope Array — Utah
notes: site:telescope-array-utah-central-site currently carries a coarser (precision_m 15000) Nominatim geocode of the town of Delta, explicitly documented there as not a survey point for the array; the array's own descriptive centre found this session is reported as a site coordinate correction candidate in the worklog.

The 507-station 1.2 km SD grid and the three fluorescence-detector sites (Black Rock Mesa, Long Ridge, Middle Drum) are not drawn: their widely repeated coordinates trace only to a hobbyist astronomy site (cleardarksky.com, also Wikipedia's own citation), not to an official TA page or paper fetched this session (telescopearray.org and known mirrors were unreachable). See worklog backlog.

summary.plain: The Telescope Array ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray observatory near Delta, Utah: 507 surface-detector stations on a 1.2 km grid over ~700 km2, watched by three fluorescence-detector stations.
summary.technical: One local map for facility:telescope-array-utah. Drawn as a single reference point at the array's own published centre (39.3N, 112.9W), tighter than the existing site record's Delta-Utah town geocode; extent_m set large (20 km) to reflect the array's true ~700 km2 scale even though only the centre point is drawn this session.
